h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ט״ז Pesach — Maamar Tes Zayin

p: הַשִּׁיר יִהְיֶה לָכֶם כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג
"You shall have a song as on the night when a festival is sanctified"
(יְשַׁעְיָה ל', כ"ט).
(Yeshayahu 30:29).
אָמַר "שִׁיר" לְשׁוֹן זָכָר, שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
It states shir ("song") in the masculine form, which is expounded in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"ג, י"א)
(Shemos Rabbah 23:11)
שֶׁכָּל הַשִּׁירוֹת לְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה וְכוּלֵּי, אֲבָל לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא אֵין עוֹד צָרוֹת וְכוּלֵּי, בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה אוֹמְרִים שִׁיר לְשׁוֹן זָכָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר

that all previous songs were in the feminine form (shirah) [because after each salvation, further troubles followed], etc., whereas in the future to come there will be no more troubles, etc., and at that time they will recite a song in the masculine form (shir), as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים צ"ו, א'):
(Tehillim 96:1):
שִׁירוּ לַה' שִׁיר חָדָשׁ.
"Sing to Hashem a new song (shir chadash)."
וְאָמַר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג,
And the verse states that this song will be "as on the night when a festival is sanctified,"
וְלֵיל זֶה נִדְרָשׁ עַל לֵיל חַג הַפֶּסַח, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּפְסָחִים
and this night is expounded as referring to the night of the festival of Pesach, as they said in Pesachim
וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא סְתָם "הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג"?
Now why is it called simply "when a festival (chag) is sanctified"?
וְכָל הַחַגִּים נִקְרְאוּ כֵּן, וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים סְתָם "חָג" הַיְינוּ חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת!
Surely all festivals are called so, and in the parlance of the Sages an unqualified chag refers to the festival of Sukkos!
וְגַם אֵין זֶה לָשׁוֹן קְצָרָה, דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "כְּלֵיל הַפֶּסַח"!
Nor is this an abbreviated expression, for it could just as easily have said "as on the night of Pesach"!
גַּם בַּתּוֹרָה אֵין מְפוֹרָשׁ חִיּוּב הַלֵּל רַק מִמִּדְרַשׁ חֲכָמִים,
Moreover, in the Written Torah the obligation of Hallel [on Pesach night] is not explicitly stated, being derived only through the exposition of the Sages
וּמַה זֶּה סִימָן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג שֶׁאוֹמְרִים בּוֹ שִׁירָה עַל לֵיל פֶּסַח?
so how is "the night when a festival is sanctified, when song is recited" a clear sign pointing specifically to Pesach night?
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן: דְּלַיְלָה זוֹ נִקְרָא לֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג בָּא מִלַּיְלָה זוֹ.
However, the explanation is that this night is called "the night when the festival is sanctified" because the entire holiness of the festival emanates from this night.
שֶׁכֵּן בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים נִקְרָא "חַג הַפֶּסַח",
For in the language of the Sages it is called "the Festival of Pesach,"
וּמִצְוַת הַקְרָבַת הַפֶּסַח הִיא בְּעֶרֶב פֶּסַח וַאֲכִילָתוֹ בְּלֵיל פֶּסַח,
even though the mitzvah of offering the Pesach sacrifice is on Erev Pesach and its eating is only on the first night of Pesach
רַק כָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג בָּא מֵחַג הַפֶּסַח,
yet the entire holiness of the seven-day festival comes from the Pesach offering,
כִּי הִיא עַל שֵׁם שֶׁפָּסַח וְכוּלֵּי שֶׁעוֹמֵד עַל הַפֶּתַח בְּכָל יְמֵי הֶחָג הַבָּאִים,
because it is named after the fact that Hashem "passed over" (pasach), etc., standing guard at the doorway throughout all the subsequent days of the festival
וְזֶה לֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג.
and this is "the night when the festival is sanctified."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ דִּכְתִיב
And as we have explained regarding what is written
(דְּבָרִים ט"ז, ג'):
(Devarim 16:3):
לֹא תֹאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ, שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת
"You shall not eat chametz with it (alav); seven days you shall eat matzos with it (alav)"
"עָלָיו" הַיְינוּ הַפֶּסַח, שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּא הַחִיּוּב לַאֲכִילַת מַצָּה וְאִיסּוּר חָמֵץ כָּל שִׁבְעָה.
"with it" refers to the Pesach offering, from which stems the obligation to eat matzah and the prohibition of chametz for all seven days.
וְכֵן בִּלְשׁוֹן תּוֹרָה נִקְרָא "חַג הַמַּצּוֹת",
And likewise in the language of the Torah it is called "the Festival of Matzos,"
וְגַם כֵּן עִיקַּר מִצְוַת מַצָּה בְּלֵיל רִאשׁוֹן דְּפֶסַח
even though the primary obligation of matzah is on the first night of Pesach
(פְּסָחִים ק"כ.),
(Pesachim 120a),
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִקְרָא כָּל הֶחָג חַג הַמַּצּוֹת שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג עִיקָּרוֹ מִלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְכָאָמוּר.
nevertheless the entire festival is called the Festival of Matzos because the essence of the festival's holiness derives from the first night, as stated.
וְאַף שֶׁחִיּוּב מַצָּה רַק לֵיל רִאשׁוֹן חוֹבָה,
And although the obligation to eat matzah is mandatory only on the first night,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת, יֵשׁ מִצְוָה בַּאֲכִילַת מַצָּה כָּל שִׁבְעָה,
nevertheless, since the Torah states "seven days you shall eat matzos with it," there is a positive mitzvah in eating matzah all seven days,
דְּאַשְׁכְּחַן
just as we find
(שָׁם קי"ד:)
(ibid. 114b)
רָבָא הֲוָה מְהַדַּר אַסִּילְקָא וְאַרוּזָא הוֹאִיל וְנָפֵיק מִפּוּמֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
that Rava would seek out beets and rice [for the Seder] simply because they were mentioned by Rav Huna,
וְכֵן
and likewise
(סוּכָּה ל"ב:)
(Sukkah 32b)
רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְהַדַּר אַתְּרֵי וְחַד הוֹאִיל וְנָפֵיק מִפּוּמֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
Rav Acha son of Rava would seek out two myrtle branches and one willow branch because it was stated by Rav Kahana
כָּל שֶׁכֵּן אֲכִילַת מַצָּה כָּל שִׁבְעָה שֶׁנִּזְכַּר בַּתּוֹרָה "שִׁבְעַת יָמִים וְגוֹמֵר" שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִצְוָה כָּל שִׁבְעָה.
how much more so is there a mitzvah in eating matzah all seven days, since it is explicitly written in the Torah "seven days, etc."
וּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא "רְשׁוּת", הַיְינוּ דְּמִצְוָה לְגַבֵּי חוֹבָה רְשׁוּת קָרֵי לֵיהּ,
And when the Gemara calls it "optional" (reshus), that is because relative to a strict obligation (chovah), an optional mitzvah is termed reshus;
וְעִיקָּרוֹ בָּא מִלֵּיל רִאשׁוֹן, דִּכְתִיב: תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת,
and its root stems from the first night, as it is written "you shall eat matzos upon it [the Pesach offering],"
וּמִזֶּה נִסְתָּעֵף לְכָל שִׁבְעָה יָמִים לְמִצְוָה לַאֲכִילַת מַצָּה, וְלָכֵן כְּתִיב: תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת.
and from this it branches out to all seven days as a mitzvah to eat matzah, which is why it is written "you shall eat matzos upon it."
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָא כָּל הֶחָג חַג הַמַּצּוֹת, וְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה מִלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
Therefore the entire festival is called the Festival of Matzos, and its holiness flows from the first night,
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא "לֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג", שֶׁכָּל קְדוּשַּׁת הַחַגִּים מִסְתָּעֲפִים מִלֵּיל זֶה.
and thus it is called "the night when the festival is sanctified," because the holiness of all the festivals branches out from this night.
שֶׁכֵּן פֶּסַח נִקְרָא רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לָרְגָלִים,
For Pesach is called the New Year for the pilgrimage festivals,
דְּ"רֹאשׁ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא רֵישָׁא לְכוּלָּא גּוּפָא, דְּבָתַר רֵישָׁא גָּרִיר,
and "head" (rosh) means that it is the head for the entire body, for the body is drawn after the head
דְּכָל הָרְגָלִים מִסְתָּעֲפִים מִקְּדוּשַּׁת חַג הַפֶּסַח, וּקְדוּשַּׁת הֶחָג הוּא עִיקָּרוֹ מִלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה.
meaning all the festivals branch out from the holiness of Pesach, and the essence of Pesach's holiness comes from the first night.
נִמְצָא דְּמִלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה נִתְקַדְּשׁוּ כָּל הַחַגִּים, וְלָכֵן קָרֵי לֵיהּ "לֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג" סְתָם.
It emerges that from this first night all the festivals were sanctified, and therefore Scripture calls it simply "the night when chag is sanctified."
וּכְתִיב "כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ" בְּכָ"ף הַדִּמְיוֹן, וּמַשְׁמַע דְּזֶה מְעוּלֶּה מִמֶּנּוּ,
And it is written "like the night when a festival is sanctified" with the comparative prefix Kaf, which implies that this night [Pesach] is even superior to that future song,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
along the lines of what they said
(תַּעֲנִית ז'.):
(Taanis 7a):
מִי נִתְלֶה בְּמִי? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר קָטָן נִתְלֶה בַּגָּדוֹל.
"Who is compared to whom? You must say the lesser is compared to the greater."
רַק לֶעָתִיד דְּיִתְבַּטֵּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לֹא יִפָּלֵא כָּל כָּךְ,
Because in the future, when the evil inclination will be abolished, [singing praise] will not be so wondrous;
אַךְ בְּלֵיל זֶה שֶׁעֲדַיִין הָיָה שְׁלִיטַת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָל שְׂאוֹר לֹא יִמָּצֵא לְבַעֵר הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה מִלֵּב כְּסִיל, זֶה הוּא פֶּלֶא יוֹתֵר.

whereas on this night of Pesach, while the evil inclination still holds sway, and yet Israel merited "no leaven shall be found" to eradicate the leaven in the dough from the fool's heart, this is an even greater wonder.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אָמַר: הַשִּׁיר דְּלֶעָתִיד יִהְיֶה גַּם כֵּן כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג שֶׁאָז נִתְבַּטֵּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
Therefore it says that the song of the future will also be like the night when the festival is sanctified, when the evil inclination was nullified
שֶׁכֵּן מוֹרֶה יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁיָּצְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵהַמֵּעִיק וּמֵיצַר לְמִדַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהָיְתָה הַקְּלִיפָּה מַקֶּפֶת אוֹתָם מִכָּל צַד.

for such is the meaning of the Exodus from Egypt, when Israel emerged from the oppressor and straits (meitzar) into the attribute of Israel, whereas previously the spiritual husk surrounded them on every side.
וְכֵן בְּכָל שָׁנָה בְּלַיְלָה זוֹ מִתְחַדֵּשׁ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַעֵר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
And so too every year on this night, a renewal occurs in the heart of Israel to eradicate the evil inclination,
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִרְאוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יָצָא מִמִּצְרַיִם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִרְגִּישׁוּ אָז הַשִּׂמְחָה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר.
for a person must view himself as though he personally went out of Egypt, and just as they felt that joy then, so must one feel it in every single generation.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 23:11 — "All the songs sung in the world are in the feminine form: just as a female conceives and gives birth and gives birth again, so troubles came upon them again and again, and they sang songs in the feminine… But in the time to come there will be no more troubles… At that hour they will say shir in the masculine, as it says, 'Sing to Hashem a new song (shir chadash).'"

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 95b — "R. Yochanan said in the name of R. Shimon ben Yehotzadak: Scripture says, 'You shall have a song as on the night when a festival is sanctified' (Yeshayahu 30:29): a night sanctified for a festival requires Hallel; a night not sanctified for a festival does not." Rashi: there is no festival night that calls for song except the night of Pesach, over its eating.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach Sheni 1 — “This is what the Gemara says in Pesachim 95b: a night sanctified for the festival requires Hallel, while the second Pesach, which is not sanctified for a festival, does not require Hallel at its eating. The wording is ‘when a festival is sanctified’ (hiskadesh chag), and not ‘sanctified for a festival,’ for then the holiness of the festival was sanctified by Hashem; that is, then the aspect of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael, came into being, when Israel accepted His kingship… and one who takes the foundation first takes the whole building.” Connection: The same reading of “hiskadesh chag” as the night from which the festival’s holiness itself begins, adding the contrast with Pesach Sheni, which has no Hallel.

The wording is ‘when a festival is sanctified’ (hiskadesh chag), and not ‘sanctified for a festival,’ for then the holiness of the festival was sanctified by Hashem; that is, then the aspect of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael, came into being, when Israel accepted His kingship… and one who takes the foundation first takes the whole building.” Connection: The same reading of “hiskadesh chag” as the night from which the festival’s holiness itself begins, adding the contrast with Pesach Sheni, which has no Hallel.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Pesach 1 — “‘On the first of Nisan is the New Year for the festivals’—but it is on the fifteenth of Nisan! Rather, the festival that falls in it is the head of the festivals. The festival of Pesach is the brain of all the festivals, because it is the first festival, coming at once at the time of the Exodus. And although the other festivals have aspects higher in rank than Pesach, in this respect Pesach is the brain of the other festivals, and they surround it.” Connection: The Apter reads “a festival in which is the New Year for the festivals,” as Rav Tzadok does, to mean that Pesach is the head from which all the festivals draw.
